objective: M1 offline OFD catalog search/custom records/provenance and safe OpenSpool NTAG215 read-write verification for the Motorola Razr 2023, with PAXX extensions behind an explicit profile.
owner_requirements: No INTERNET permission, accounts, telemetry, backend, live catalog download, OPT, Spoolman, printer command, firmware change, tag locking, or publishing.
Reject malformed, oversized, duplicate-key, unsupported-version, unknown-field, invalid-range, and legacy diameter 175 payloads without silent coercion.

Freeze write bytes; bind overwrite consent to UID and existing content; durably journal before the platform write; use UNKNOWN after interruption; reconcile read-only on same UID; verify exactly one matching MIME NDEF record.
Keep immutable bundled OFD data separate from mutable user records; deterministic generation; atomic transactional import/recovery.
Physical device, NTAG215, PAXX/U1, independent-reader, and performance acceptance remain host/human gates.
implementation_summary: Strict JSON now limits bytes/depth/number length, ASCII number digits, duplicate keys, UTF-8, and surrogate pairing.

Codec validates mandatory exact JSON types, strings, color, decimal-mm diameter, bounded integer-string temperatures, weight, additional colors, unknown fields/version, reports actual omissions, and treats alpha as loss-preserving read-only.
Intent, UID, and record byte arrays are defensively frozen. Length-delimited consent fingerprints bind UID plus all existing NDEF record TNF/type/payload data.

Coordinator serializes NFC work, refuses unsupported existing OpenSpool replacement, journals UID/payload synchronously before write, restores UNKNOWN after process death, reads fresh, and verifies full one-record framing.

Bundled catalog manifest and SHA-256 are validated before a transactional Room replacement; custom data remains in a separate database. UI exposes offline search, exact package metadata, profile/omission preview, custom persistence, recents recording, decoded-tag local editing, and NFC state.
local_evidence: Independent Kotlin compiler completed for all core main sources.

JUnit 4.13.2: 21 focused core tests passed, including malformed codec inputs, actual omission reporting, immutability, consent-content changes, UID mismatch, extra/wrong NDEF records, UNKNOWN restore, and catalog replacement rollback.
Catalog tool generated 22347 packages, 1754819 bytes, SHA-256 1f1fa47e630ee52e1ea2511d5cd012faa472edac04f5c74194e3f646d2d1ba89; generated gzip was byte-identical to bundled asset.
Manifest JSON parsed, package count and digest matched, and exactly one representative SUNLU ABS Orange/FF8E24/1.75/1000 hit was present.
Android manifest and backup-rule XML parsed; android.permission.INTERNET was absent.
limitations: The worker could not initiate the protected Gradle command because heavy-gradle could not create its read-only /mnt/faststorage/build-work cache. Build artifacts appeared during the run but were not accepted as worker-attributable final evidence because source continued changing; host must run the exact command before review closure.
No accepted final APK/lint evidence, instrumentation, 2023 Razr UI, NFC tag, interruption, RF-removal persistence, PAXX/U1, independent-reader, or on-device p95 evidence exists yet.
The review package is advisory input only; no independent reviewer cycle has run for this source.

review_questions.claude: Is the write lifecycle, storage separation, and immutable intent design maintainable and correctly bounded?
review_questions.gemini: Does the Android NDEF/Room/Compose implementation agree with current platform contracts and the PAXX/OpenSpool target?
review_questions.deepseek: Find failure modes that could falsely verify, overwrite changed content, lose UNKNOWN state, accept malformed input, corrupt catalog state, or mislead UI acceptance.
